independent.summary: The catch-up arm keys off `leoRefreshLastRun`, which `runRefreshForEntity` only stamps on success (line 184; the failure path at line 208 just logs), so an entity whose rescrape throws — Puppeteer launch failure, site down hard, a Mongo error in `persistRescrapeResult` — becomes due again every single hour once the stale stamp passes the 26h window (26h, 27h, 28h…), turning one failed daily refresh into an indefinite hourly re-crawl with full Puppeteer + embedding cost; before this change a failed run simply waited for the next day's scheduled hour.

In the re-entrancy test the second tick is fired at `AT_SLOT + HOUR` (04:00) against an entity with `leoRefreshLastRun: null` and hour 3, so that entity is `awaiting-first-slot` and would not crawl at that time even with the guard removed — the `rescrapeCalls === 1` assertion that the comment presents as proving "two overlapping calls put exactly ONE crawl in flight" is vacuous (only the `second.ran/reason` assertions actually exercise the flag).

triageGrades.reason: The diff touches only the scheduler predicate, its tick and a log-level env example — no authentication, session, role or permission code.
The only .env.example addition is `LEO_REFRESH_LOG_LEVEL`, a log-verbosity knob; no credential, key or secret handling is introduced or changed.
No billing, pricing, quota or Stripe code is touched by the diff.
The diff adds no delete/overwrite logic — `rescrapeSite` and `persistRescrapeResult` are untouched and only invoked as before.
No external API call site is added or modified in the diff; it only decides when the existing refresh path runs.
Nothing release-related changes — no CI, deploy config, version bump or migration — and a new unit-test file is not release surface.
